To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conductance of apple leaves can be predicted with an accuracy of 60-65% by a model that involves air vapour pressure, air temperature and irradiance.

the conductance of apple leaves is well predicted by a simple model involving air temperature, air vapour pressure, soil water content and irradiance, and that the model parameters are stable over years and sites.

(i) leaf conductance is best predicted from air temperature, vapour pressure deficit and soil moisture deficit; and (ii) the model parameters are cultivar and age dependent, but are relatively stable over time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of models of the leaf conductance of apple orchards.
the development of a general model of the conductance (gl ) of leaves in apple trees ( Malus domestica Borkh.).
developing a simple model for predicting gl in orchard trees, based only on environmental variables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a simple hyperbolic function involving vapour pressure deficit and air temperature, together with soil moisture deficit, is the best model of gl in the apple orchard environment.

the simple empirical model of leaf conductance proposed here should be used as a basis for future studies, but that soil moisture deficit should be included among the independent variables in order to improve the predictive power of the model.
a simple model of gl involving air vapour deficit, temperature and irradiance is a good predictor of the seasonal variation in gl for apple leaves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
leaf conductance can be predicted from a small number of environmental variables, but that the optimal set of variables and their functional relationships vary with location and season.
the best model for predicting leaf conductances in apple orchards was the hyperbolic model, with soil moisture deficit as an optional additional variable.
the most important environmental variables for the prediction of leaf conductance in apple orchards are vapour pressure deficit and air temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple model of the type described here is sufficient to explain most of the variation in leaf conductance in the field.
it is possible to develop simple, predictive models for leaf conductance that work across different cultivars, sites and years, using only environmental measurements.
a simple model can be effective in predicting the variation in gl over a large range of environmental conditions and for different cultivars.
